tasks.title: Network board: bridge, veth, VLAN
tasks.statement: Build the network of a Linux host the way an administrator does: namespaces, veth pairs, bridges, virtual machine ports and VLAN tags. The board works out which interfaces have a link, which segment each address is in and whether a ping gets through. Five scenarios: put a bridge between two containers, separate two groups of machines with VLANs on one bridge, find a port with a foreign tag, find a virtual machine on the wrong bridge and bring up a veth end that is down. The exercise is solved when all scenarios are solved.
tasks.hint: Select an interface and read its state and the reason on the right. A veth end is alive only while its peer end is alive. Bridge ports with different VLAN tags are different segments; the tag is set in the parameters of the port, and the address belongs to the bridge or the machine itself, not to the port.
